name: Given a set A of positive integers whose reciprocal
notes:
Auto-designed from: Design an Ob3ect for:

Given a set A of positive integers whose reciprocal sum diverges determine whether A contains ari

phase_0.boundary_condition: the set A of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum
phase_0.domain_name: Given a set A of positive integers whose reciprocal
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: the map from A to its partial reciprocal sums
AFWD.justification: a directed transformation that advances from finite initial segments toward the infinite sum

AREV.chosen_element: the descent from an arithmetic progression back to its common difference and starting term
AREV.justification: a reverse transformation that decomposes a found progression into its generating parameters

CLINK.chosen_element: chaining the divergence test with the progression search
CLINK.justification: sequential composition where the output of the reciprocal-sum check feeds the progression enumerator

ENGAGR.chosen_element: A both contains progressions of every finite length and is bounded by a finite maximum length
ENGAGR.justification: the B state where the affirmative and negative findings are held simultaneously without resolution

EVALF.chosen_element: A contains no arithmetic progression beyond some fixed finite length
EVALF.justification: the negative state constructively refuted by identifying a maximum length that bounds all progressions in A

EVALT.chosen_element: A contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length
EVALT.justification: the affirmative state constructively proven by exhibiting progressions of unbounded length

FFUSE.chosen_element: the rejoined verdict on the progression property of A
FFUSE.justification: the two arms rejoin into a single resolved state; if one arm affirms progressions of every length and the other affirms a finite cap, the contradiction fuses to B

FSPLIT.chosen_element: the decision on whether A contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions
FSPLIT.justification: one state opens into two arms: one arm searches for progressions of every finite length, the other arm searches for a maximum finite length beyond which no progression exists

IFIX.chosen_element: the final verdict recorded on the progression property of A
IFIX.justification: a permanent append-only fixation that cannot be undone once the kernel returns its B4 value

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: the identity of set A as the object under test
IMSCRIB.justification: self-reference that leaves A unchanged while confirming it is the same set throughout

TANCH.chosen_element: the closed system of all subsets of positive integers whose reciprocal sum diverges
TANCH.justification: the terminal boundary that contains every candidate set A under test

VINIT.chosen_element: empty set A with no members named
VINIT.justification: the void state before any positive integer is admitted into A

phase_2.fuse_element: the rejoined verdict on the progression property of A
phase_2.fuse_result: a single B4 state over SIXTEEN_3 that may be N, T, F, or B depending on what the arms establish
phase_2.rejoin_note: the first arm enumerates progressions of increasing length and affirms each; the second arm attempts to bound all progressions by a fixed length; the arms rejoin into one state, and if both establish their claims the fork closes to B
phase_2.split_element: the decision on whether A contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions
phase_2.split_input: set A with divergent reciprocal sum
split_outputs: arm affirming progressions of every finite length
arm affirming a finite maximum progression length
phase_2.verdict_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.both_description: B4 B (11) — both held at once: a live contradiction, the paraconsistent resolution
phase_3.void_description: B4 N (00) — neither: uninitialized, nothing established

steps.domain_action: set A is uninitialized with no positive integers named
form partial reciprocal sums over finite initial segments of A
confirm the reciprocal sum over A diverges
assert A is the same set under test throughout
branch on whether A contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length
exhibit arithmetic progressions in A of unbounded finite length
identify a fixed finite length that bounds all arithmetic progressions in A
hold both the unbounded progression claim and the finite bound claim simultaneously
rejoin the two arms into a single resolved state over SIXTEEN_3
permanently record the B4 verdict on the progression property of A
seal the closed system containing the final verdict

phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical store of known sets with divergent reciprocal sums and their progression structures
phase_5.compiler_frontend: translates the divergence and progression queries into IMASM token operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: passes partial sums and progression witnesses between the split arms
phase_5.memory_mechanism: stores the set A, its partial reciprocal sums, and discovered progressions
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: orders the divergence check before the progression search and the fuse after both arms

phase_6.cycle_cost: the computational work of summing reciprocals and enumerating progressions per cycle
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — the cycle transforms information without creating or destroying state, only resolving it into a B4 register
phase_6.post_cycle_state: set A with a fixed B4 verdict on its progression property
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: set A with unnamed members and no established progression property
